g1.label: 1. Passed down from ___ to generation
g1.why: The text says folk songs were passed down from generation to generation.

g2.label: 2. Told stories of ___ life
g2.why: The text says folk songs often told stories of ordinary life.

g3.label: 3. A Celtic folk instrument
g3.why: The text names the bagpipes as a distinctive Celtic folk instrument.

g4.label: 4. Often played in a crowded ___
g4.why: The text says folk music is often played in a small, crowded pub.

g5.label: 5. Modern bands combine folk with a more ___ sound
g5.why: The text says modern bands combine folk with a more modern sound.

g6.label: 6. Focus on honest ___
g6.why: The text says folk-inspired music keeps its focus on honest lyrics.

g7.label: 7. Some argue folk-inspired pop is not ___ folk music
g7.why: The text says some argue folk-inspired pop is not real folk music.

g8.label: 8. Both sides agree the tradition is ___
g8.why: The text says both sides agree the folk tradition is alive.

g1.label: 1. One of the ___ forms of music (old)
g1.why: ‘One of the ___’ always takes the superlative form: oldest.

g2.label: 2. Pop is often ___ than folk (polished)
g2.why: Longer adjectives like ‘polished’ form the comparative with ‘more’.

g3.label: 3. A pub is ___ than a hall (small)
g3.why: Short adjectives like ‘small’ form the comparative by adding ‘-er’.

g4.label: 4. The bagpipes are ___ than the fiddle (loud)
g4.why: Short adjectives like ‘loud’ form the comparative by adding ‘-er’.

g5.label: 5. The ___ song on the album (good)
g5.why: ‘Good’ is irregular: its superlative form is ‘best’.

g6.label: 6. Modern folk is ___ than traditional (commercial)
g6.why: Longer adjectives like ‘commercial’ form the comparative with ‘more’.

g7.label: 7. One of the ___ singers (famous)
g7.why: ‘One of the ___’ always takes the superlative form, and longer adjectives use ‘most’.

g8.label: 8. Live folk feels ___ than a recording (authentic)
g8.why: Longer adjectives like ‘authentic’ form the comparative with ‘more’.

g1.label: 1. A pub is not ___ a concert hall
g1.why: The negative equative structure is ‘not as + adjective + as’.

g2.label: 2. ___ classical music is formal, folk is relaxed
g2.why: ‘Whereas’ introduces a direct contrast between two clauses.

g3.label: 3. ___ Mumford & Sons and Ed Sheeran use folk sounds
g3.why: ‘Both X and Y’ links two similar subjects.

g4.label: 4. ___ pop songs, folk songs have no known writer
g4.why: ‘Unlike’ + noun introduces a contrast at the start of a sentence.

g5.label: 5. Folk is just ___ popular today as before
g5.why: The equative structure is ‘just as + adjective + as’.

g6.label: 6. The fiddle, ___ the violin, has four strings
g6.why: ‘Like’ + noun shows similarity between two things.

g7.label: 7. ___ side wants the tradition to die
g7.why: ‘Neither’ + singular noun + singular verb expresses ‘not one nor the other’.

g8.label: 8. Folk is very different ___ commercial pop
g8.why: The fixed phrase is ‘different from’, not ‘different than’ in standard British English.
